drug_name: Acetaminophen, Dextromethorphan Hydrobromide, Guaifenesin, and Doxylamine
brand_names: Mucinex Fast-Max Night Time Cold & Flu
Robitussin Nighttime Severe Multi-Symptom Cough Cold & Flu
what_its_for: This combination medicine is used to relieve nighttime cold and flu symptoms all at once. Acetaminophen reduces fever and eases pain (like headaches, body aches, and sore throat). Dextromethorphan helps quiet a nagging cough. Guaifenesin loosens and thins mucus so it is easier to cough up. Doxylamine is an antihistamine that helps dry up a runny nose, sneezing, and also makes you feel drowsy so you can get a better night's rest.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a small snack or glass of milk. Use only the measuring cup or spoon that comes with the package — never use a kitchen spoon, as it may give you the wrong amount. Swallow tablets or capsules whole with a full glass of water. Drink plenty of extra fluids throughout the day to help loosen mucus. Because doxylamine causes drowsiness, take this medicine only at bedtime or when you do not need to drive or operate machinery.
dosing: Adults and children 12 years and older: Take the dose listed on the product label (this varies slightly by brand). A typical adult dose is taken once every 6 hours as needed, but do not take more than 4 doses in 24 hours. Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg per day for healthy adults; 2,000 mg per day if you drink alcohol regularly). Children under 12: Do not use this product unless specifically directed by a doctor. Always read the label of your specific product for the exact dose.
missed_dose: This medicine is taken only as needed for cold and flu symptoms, so there is no set schedule. If you miss a dose and you still have symptoms, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue as normal. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one, as this could give you too much acetaminophen, which can be harmful.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture — do not store in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Check the expiration date on the package and throw away any medicine that has expired. Do not flush medicines down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine. Alcohol increases the risk of liver damage from acetaminophen and makes drowsiness from doxylamine much worse. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you — it can cause significant drowsiness. Do not take any other medicines that contain acetaminophen (such as Tylenol or other cold, flu, or pain products) at the same time, as this can lead to a dangerous overdose. Avoid taking with sleep aids, sedatives, anxiety medicines, muscle relaxers, or other antihistamines without first talking to your doctor or pharmacist. Do not take MAO inhibitors (such as phenelzine, selegiline, or linezolid) within 14 days of using this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency help right away if you: take more than the recommended dose accidentally; notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (signs of liver problems); develop a rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing (signs of an allergic reaction); have a cough that lasts more than 7 days, keeps coming back, or is accompanied by a rash or long-lasting headache; have a fever above 103°F (39.4°C) or a fever that lasts more than 3 days; feel extremely confused, have trouble urinating, or notice a fast or irregular heartbeat. Also call your doctor before use if you have liver disease, kidney disease, glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, a chronic cough (from asthma, smoking, or emphysema), or if you take blood thinners like warfarin.
when_it_works: You may begin to feel relief within 30 minutes to 1 hour after taking a dose. Fever reduction and pain relief often happen first. The drowsy effect of doxylamine typically sets in within 30 minutes, which is why this medicine is best taken at bedtime. Cough and congestion relief may take a little longer. This medicine treats your symptoms temporarily — it does not cure a cold or the flu. Most cold and flu symptoms improve on their own within 7 to 10 days.
special_populations: Older adults (65+): Use with caution. Doxylamine can cause increased confusion, dizziness, falls, and difficulty urinating in older adults. Talk to your doctor before using this product. Pregnancy: Do not use without first talking to your doctor or midwife. Breastfeeding: Avoid this medicine while breastfeeding, as doxylamine and other ingredients can pass into breast milk and may harm your baby. Children under 12: Do not use this product. Use only children's products specifically labeled for their age and weight. People with liver disease: Avoid this product or use only under close medical supervision, as acetaminophen can worsen liver problems. People who regularly drink 3 or more alcoholic drinks per day: Talk to your doctor before using, due to the increased risk of liver damage from acetaminophen.
